items.title: Taking away a mixed number
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $3\tfrac{1}{3} - 1\tfrac{3}{4}$? Give a fraction.

widget.accept: Any form equal to $\tfrac{19}{12}$, which is $1\tfrac{7}{12}$

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write each mixed number as a single fraction, then use a common denominator.

byKey.smaller-from-larger: You took $\tfrac{1}{3}$ from $\tfrac{3}{4}$ because it was easier. The sum asks for $\tfrac{1}{3} - \tfrac{3}{4}$, which borrows from the whole 2.

explain.text: As single fractions, $3\tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{10}{3}$ and $1\tfrac{3}{4} = \tfrac{7}{4}$. Over twelfths that is $\tfrac{40}{12} - \tfrac{21}{12} = \tfrac{19}{12}$. That is $1\tfrac{7}{12}$.

items.title: Building 39%
items.prose: Work without a calculator. A desk keeps 39% of a £360 commission.
items.question: What is 39% of £360, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find 10% and 1%, then build 40% and take 1% away.

byKey.tenth: You found 3.9%. Moving the point once more gives 39%.
byKey.forty: You found 40%. Take away 1%, which is £3.60.
byKey.added-one: You added 1% to 40%. 39% is 1% less than 40%.

items.title: Falling further below zero
items.prose: A desk's P&L is −£3k at noon. By the close it has fallen by another £5k.
items.question: Drag the point to the P&L at the close, in £k.

feedback.correct: Five more to the left of −3.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. A fall moves left. Start at −3 and move 5 to the left.

byKey.rose: You moved 5 to the right, which is a rise. A fall moves left.
byKey.ignored-start: You worked out $3 - 5$. The start is −3, so the fall takes it to −8.
byKey.p: Start at −3 and count 5 steps to the left.

explain.text: A fall of £5k is a move of 5 to the left. From −3 that lands on −8. In symbols, $-3 - 5 = -8$.

items.title: Five prices in order
items.prose: Five fills of a cheap share, in pounds.
items.question: Put the prices in order, smallest first.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the tenths digit first, then the hundredths.

byKey.d45: You placed 0.45 too early because it has fewer digits. As 0.450 it is the largest.
byKey.d0455: You read 0.0455 as large because of its digits. It has 0 tenths, so it is the smallest.

explain.text: Two prices have 0 tenths, so they are smallest: 0.0455 has 4 hundredths and 0.054 has 5. Among the rest, 0.4 is 0.400, then 0.405, then 0.450. More digits do not make a number bigger.

items.title: Pounds against pence
items.prose: A share trade costs a £1.20 commission, 45p of stamp duty and a 15p exchange fee.
items.question: Write commission : stamp duty : exchange fee in its simplest form.

options.why: You compared 1.20 with 45 and 15 without matching units. That sets pounds against pence.
You reversed the order. The commission comes first.
You stopped early. 24, 9 and 3 still share a factor of 3.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write all three in pence, then divide by the highest common factor.

explain.text: £1.20 is 120p, so the ratio is $120 : 45 : 15$. All three divide by 15, giving $8 : 3 : 1$.

items.title: What the tranches leave
items.prose: Work without a calculator. A fund splits £$4\tfrac{1}{2}$ million into tranches of £$\tfrac{5}{8}$ million each. It issues only full tranches.
items.question: How much is left over, in millions of pounds? Give a fraction.

widget.accept: Any form equal to $\tfrac{1}{8}$, which is £125,000

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find how many tranches fit, keep the whole number, then subtract what they use.

byKey.tranche-share: You gave the $\tfrac{1}{5}$ left from $7\tfrac{1}{5}$. That is a fifth of a tranche, and a tranche is $\tfrac{5}{8}$ million.
byKey.count: You gave the number of full tranches. The question asks for the money left over.
byKey.count-exact: You gave how many tranches fit. Only 7 are full, so find what is left.
byKey.multiplied: You multiplied the two amounts. How many fit is a division.

explain.text: $\tfrac{9}{2} \times \tfrac{8}{5} = \tfrac{36}{5} = 7\tfrac{1}{5}$, so 7 tranches are full. They use $7 \times \tfrac{5}{8} = \tfrac{35}{8} = 4\tfrac{3}{8}$ million. That leaves $4\tfrac{4}{8} - 4\tfrac{3}{8} = \tfrac{1}{8}$ million.

items.title: Which decimals stop
items.question: Which of these fractions give a decimal that stops, called a terminating decimal? Select all that apply.

options.why: You saw the 8 in $24 = 8 \times 3$. The 3 makes it recur: $\tfrac{7}{24} = 0.291666\ldots$
You saw the 10 in 30. Its factor of 3 stays after simplifying, so $\tfrac{11}{30} = 0.3666\ldots$ recurs.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Simplify each fraction, then look for prime factors other than 2 and 5 in the denominator.

explain.text: In lowest terms, a decimal stops when the denominator has only the prime factors 2 and 5. $\tfrac{9}{75} = \tfrac{3}{25}$ and $\tfrac{21}{56} = \tfrac{3}{8}$ pass once simplified. The denominators 24 and 30 keep a factor of 3.

items.title: Ticks in a big move
items.prose: Work without a calculator. A futures price moves in ticks worth $\text{£}8 \times 10^{-3}$ each. A position's value has moved by $\text{£}6 \times 10^{5}$.
items.question: How many ticks is that? Give the answer in standard form.

options.why: You divided correctly but stopped. Standard form needs a first number from 1 up to 10.
You moved the power the wrong way when you turned 0.75 into 7.5. The power must drop by one.
You added the powers. Dividing subtracts them: $5 - (-3) = 8$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the numbers, subtract the powers, then tidy into standard form.

items.title: A root, then a square
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $\left(\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{8}{27}}\right)^2$? Give a fraction.

feedback.correct: The cube root is $\tfrac{2}{3}$, and its square is $\tfrac{4}{9}$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the fraction whose cube is $\tfrac{8}{27}$, then square it.

byKey.top-only: You took the cube root of the 8 only. The 27 needs it too: $3^3 = 27$.
byKey.doubled: You doubled $\tfrac{2}{3}$. Squaring multiplies it by itself.
byKey.no-root: You squared $\tfrac{8}{27}$ without taking the cube root first.

explain.text: $\tfrac{2}{3} \times \tfrac{2}{3} \times \tfrac{2}{3} = \tfrac{8}{27}$, so the cube root is $\tfrac{2}{3}$. Squaring gives $\tfrac{2}{3} \times \tfrac{2}{3} = \tfrac{4}{9}$.

items.title: Which operation first
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $20 - 4 \times (1 - 4)^2 \div 6$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Brackets, then powers, then multiply and divide, then subtract.

byKey.left-to-right: You did $20 - 4$ first. Multiplying and dividing come before subtracting.
byKey.negative-square: You squared −3 to get −9. A negative times a negative is positive, so it is 9.

explain.text: The bracket is −3, and its square is 9. Then $4 \times 9 \div 6 = 6$. Last comes the subtraction: $20 - 6 = 14$.

items.title: An estimate first
items.prose: Estimate $\dfrac{9.62 \times 0.0487}{0.00213}$ without a calculator.
items.question: Round each number to 1 significant figure. What is your estimate?

options.why: You rounded 9.62 down to 9. To one significant figure it rounds up to 10.
You rounded 0.0487 to 0.5. Its first significant figure is in the hundredths, so it rounds to 0.05.
You multiplied by 0.002 instead of dividing by it.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Round each number to its first significant figure, then work it out.

explain.text: The numbers round to 10, 0.05 and 0.002. Then $10 \times 0.05 = 0.5$ and $0.5 \div 0.002 = 250$. A calculator gives about 220, so the estimate is the right size.

items.title: The price before two moves
items.prose: A share falls 15%, then rises 20%. It is now priced at £306.
items.question: What was the price before the two moves, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Combine the two multipliers into one, then divide by it.

byKey.net-five: You added the moves to a 5% rise and divided by 1.05. The moves multiply: $0.85 \times 1.2 = 1.02$.
byKey.one-move: You undid only the fall. Undo the 20% rise too.
byKey.net-five-off: You took 5% off £306. The moves multiply to 1.02, so divide by 1.02.
byKey.reapplied: You applied both moves again. To go back, divide by the multipliers.

explain.text: The two moves multiply the price by $0.85 \times 1.2 = 1.02$, so $1.02p = 306$. Dividing gives $p = 300$. Check: £300 falls to £255, and a 20% rise takes it to £306.

items.title: Three moves in a row
items.prose: A portfolio falls 30%, then rises 20%, then rises 25%.
items.question: What is the overall percentage change?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn each change into a multiplier and multiply them.

byKey.added: You added the percentages: $-30 + 20 + 25$. Each change acts on a new value, so multiply.
byKey.multiplier: You typed the overall multiplier as a percentage. 105% of the start is a 5% rise.

explain.text: The multipliers are 0.7, 1.2 and 1.25. Their product is $0.7 \times 1.2 \times 1.25 = 1.05$, a rise of 5%. Adding the moves would wrongly give 15%.

items.title: From the gap to the whole
items.prose: Three desks share a bonus in the ratio $6 : 3 : 2$. Desk A gets £960 more than desk C.
items.question: What is the whole bonus, in pounds?

feedback.correct: A and C differ by 4 parts, so one part is £240 and 11 parts are £2,640.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The gap between the shares is a number of parts. Find one part first.

byKey.a-minus-b: You used the gap between A and B, 3 parts. The £960 is the gap between A and C, 4 parts.
byKey.gap-as-share: You treated £960 as desk A's share. It is the difference between A and C.
byKey.gap-as-total: You gave the gap. The question asks for the whole bonus.
byKey.two-desks: You counted only A's and C's parts. Desk B's 3 parts are in the bonus too.

explain.text: The gap between A and C is $6 - 2 = 4$ parts, so one part is $960 \div 4 = 240$. The whole bonus is $6 + 3 + 2 = 11$ parts: $11 \times 240 = 2640$. The shares are £1,440, £720 and £480.

items.title: Through the pound
items.prose: The quoted rates: £1 buys 1.25 US dollars, and £1 buys €1.15. A bond pays a 500 US dollar coupon, and a broker charges a €1,840 fee.
items.question: Fill in the table.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. To turn a foreign amount into pounds, divide by its rate.

byKey.r0c1: Each pound is worth more than a dollar, so there are fewer pounds than dollars. Divide 500 by 1.25.
byKey.r0c2: Go through pounds: turn the dollars into pounds, then multiply by 1.15.
byKey.r1c1: Each pound buys €1.15, so there are fewer pounds than euros. Divide 1,840 by 1.15.

explain.text: Each pound buys 1.25 dollars, so 500 dollars is $500 \div 1.25 = 400$ pounds. In euros that is $400 \times 1.15 = 460$. The fee is $1840 \div 1.15 = 1600$ pounds.

items.title: What share lost
items.prose: Of 1,250 trades last month, 85 lost money.
items.question: What percentage of the trades lost money?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the part by the whole, then turn the decimal into a percentage.

byKey.flipped: You divided 1,250 by 85. Put the part over the whole.
byKey.decimal: You typed the decimal 0.068. As a percentage that is 6.8%.

explain.text: The part is 85 and the whole is 1,250. $\tfrac{85}{1250} = \tfrac{6.8}{100}$, which is 6.8%. Check: 10% of 1,250 is 125, and 85 is about two thirds of that.

items.title: A steady fill
items.prose: An algorithm buys 1,800 shares in 2.5 minutes, at a steady rate.
items.question: At the same rate, how many seconds does it take to buy 4,500 shares?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the shares bought per second, then divide 4,500 by it.

byKey.minutes: You found 6.25 minutes. The question asks for seconds.

explain.text: 2.5 minutes is 150 seconds, so the rate is $1800 \div 150 = 12$ shares a second. Then $4500 \div 12 = 375$ seconds. That is 6.25 minutes.

items.title: Three years of losses
items.prose: A trading server loses 20% of its value each year. After 3 years it is worth £10,240.
items.question: What was the server worth when new, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each year multiplies the value by 0.8. Undo three of those.

byKey.simple: You took off 60% in one go. Each 20% is taken from a smaller value, so the losses are not 3 equal amounts.
byKey.added-back: You added 20% back each year. Each loss was 20% of a larger value, so divide by 0.8.

explain.text: Each year keeps 80% of the value, so after 3 years the value is $0.8^3 = 0.512$ of the price new. Then $10240 \div 0.512 = 20000$. Check: 20,000, 16,000, 12,800, 10,240.

items.title: Inverse proportion both ways
items.prose: $y$ is inversely proportional to $x$. When $x = 2$, $y = 12$.
items.question: Fill in the missing values.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. In inverse proportion $xy$ stays the same. Find it from the given pair first.

byKey.direct-3: You scaled $y$ up with $x$. In inverse proportion a bigger $x$ gives a smaller $y$.
byKey.direct-5: You multiplied $y$ by $\tfrac{5}{2}$. Keep the product fixed instead: $5y = 24$.
byKey.direct-x: You treated the link as direct. A large $y$ needs a small $x$: $40x = 24$.

explain.text: The product is $xy = 2 \times 12 = 24$, so $y = \tfrac{24}{x}$. Then $y$ is 8 at $x = 3$ and 4.8 at $x = 5$. For $y = 40$, $x = \tfrac{24}{40} = 0.6$.

items.title: Signs and powers
items.question: Which of these are equal to −8? Select all that apply.

options.why: The power touches only the 4, so $-4^2 = -16$. Then $-16 \div (-2) = 8$.
You stopped at $(-2)^3 = -8$. The minus in front turns it into 8.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out the power first, then any minus sign written in front of it.

items.title: Two ratios joined
items.prose: Desks A, B and C share a £1,400 bonus. $A : B = 2 : 3$ and $B : C = 4 : 5$.
items.question: How much does C get, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Make B the same number of parts in both ratios first.

byKey.joined: You wrote $2 : 3 : 5$ and added the parts. B is 3 parts in one ratio and 4 in the other, so match B first.
byKey.two-only: You shared the £1,400 between B and C alone. A takes a share too.

explain.text: B is 3 parts in one ratio and 4 in the other, so scale both to 12: $A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15$. That is 35 parts, so one part is $1400 \div 35 = 40$. C gets $15 \times 40 = 600$.

items.title: Fees on the way in and out
items.prose: You put £10,000 into a fund. It takes a 1.5% entry fee first, and the rest grows by 12%. Then the fund keeps 20% of any value above the £10,000 you paid in.
items.question: How much do you end with, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take each step in order: the entry fee, the growth, then 20% of the value above £10,000.

byKey.skipped-entry: You grew the whole £10,000. The entry fee comes off before anything is invested.
byKey.fee-on-growth: You charged 20% on all the growth. The fee is only on the value above the £10,000 you paid in.
byKey.fee-on-all: You took 20% of the whole value. The fee is 20% of the part above £10,000.

explain.text: After the 1.5% fee, £9,850 is invested, and 12% growth makes $9850 \times 1.12 = 11032$. The value above £10,000 is £1,032, and 20% of it is £206.40. You keep $11032 - 206.40 = 10825.60$.

items.title: Two recurring decimals, one that stops
items.prose: Both $\tfrac{5}{6} = 0.8333\ldots$ and $\tfrac{7}{15} = 0.4666\ldots$ are recurring decimals. Show that their sum is the decimal 1.3, which stops. Two of the lines do not belong.
items.question: Put the five steps in order and leave out the two that do not belong.

lines.text: In lowest terms the denominator is $10 = 2 \times 5$, so the decimal stops.

lines.why: You added tops and bottoms. That does not add the amounts, so rename both over 30 first.

lines.text: Both parts recur, so their sum must recur too.
lines.why: That is the claim the proof overturns. The factor 3 in the denominators cancels once the sum is in lowest terms.

feedback.correct: Rename over 30, add, cancel the 3, then read the denominator.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each line needs the ones before it, and two lines are false steps.

byKey.left-out: Every line but two belongs. Only the tops-and-bottoms sum and the claim that the sum must recur stay out.
byKey.add: You added before renaming. The fractions need a common denominator first.
byKey.rule: Read the denominator only once the fraction is in lowest terms. Cancel the 3 first.

explain.text: Over 30 the sum is $\tfrac{25}{30} + \tfrac{14}{30} = \tfrac{39}{30}$. Cancelling 3 gives $\tfrac{13}{10}$, whose denominator has only the factors 2 and 5. So the sum is 1.3, although neither part stops.
